cards.front: What are the common properties of metals?
cards.back: Shiny when polished, hard, strong and good conductors of heat and electricity.
cards.say: What are the common properties of metals? Shiny when polished, hard, strong and good conductors of heat and electricity.

cards.front: malleable
cards.back: Able to be hammered or bent into shapes without breaking. Most metals are malleable.
cards.say: malleable. Able to be hammered or bent into shapes without breaking. Most metals are malleable.

cards.front: ductile
cards.back: Able to be stretched into thin wires. Copper is ductile.
cards.say: ductile. Able to be stretched into thin wires. Copper is ductile.

cards.front: thermal conductor
cards.back: A material that lets heat pass through it easily. Metals are good thermal conductors.
cards.say: thermal conductor. A material that lets heat pass through it easily. Metals are good thermal conductors.

cards.front: thermal insulator
cards.back: A material that does not let heat pass through easily. Wood and plastic are thermal insulators.
cards.say: thermal insulator. A material that does not let heat pass through easily. Wood and plastic are thermal insulators.

cards.front: electrical conductor
cards.back: A material that lets electricity pass through it easily. Metals are electrical conductors.
cards.say: electrical conductor. A material that lets electricity pass through it easily. Metals are electrical conductors.

cards.front: electrical insulator
cards.back: A material that does not let electricity pass through. Plastic, rubber and glass are insulators.
cards.say: electrical insulator. A material that does not let electricity pass through. Plastic, rubber and glass are insulators.

cards.front: Why are electrical wires made of copper?
cards.back: Copper is an excellent conductor of electricity and ductile enough to be drawn into wires.
cards.say: Why are electrical wires made of copper? Copper is an excellent conductor of electricity and ductile enough to be drawn into wires.

cards.front: Why is plastic used to cover electrical wires?
cards.back: Plastic is an insulator, so it stops the electricity escaping and keeps people safe.
cards.say: Why is plastic used to cover electrical wires? Plastic is an insulator, so it stops the electricity escaping and keeps people safe.

cards.front: Why are saucepans made of metal but their handles of plastic or wood?
cards.back: The metal conducts heat to cook the food. The handle is an insulator so it does not burn your hand.
cards.say: Why are saucepans made of metal but their handles of plastic or wood? The metal conducts heat to cook the food. The handle is an insulator so it does not burn your hand.

cards.front: Are all metals magnetic?
cards.back: No. Only a few, such as iron, steel, nickel and cobalt.
cards.say: Are all metals magnetic? No. Only a few, such as iron, steel, nickel and cobalt.

cards.front: Which metal is a liquid at room temperature?
cards.back: Mercury.
cards.say: Which metal is a liquid at room temperature? Mercury.

cards.front: Why is aluminium used for aeroplanes?
cards.back: It is strong but light.
cards.say: Why is aluminium used for aeroplanes? It is strong but light.

cards.front: How can you stop iron from rusting?
cards.back: Cover it with paint, oil or plastic, or coat it with a layer of another metal.
cards.say: How can you stop iron from rusting? Cover it with paint, oil or plastic, or coat it with a layer of another metal.

cards.front: Why is gold used for jewellery?
cards.back: It is shiny, it does not rust and it is easy to shape.
cards.say: Why is gold used for jewellery? It is shiny, it does not rust and it is easy to shape.

cards.front: alloy
cards.back: A mixture of a metal with other substances. Steel is an alloy of iron.
cards.say: alloy. A mixture of a metal with other substances. Steel is an alloy of iron.

cards.front: Why is steel used for building bridges?
cards.back: It is very strong and hard.
cards.say: Why is steel used for building bridges? It is very strong and hard.

cards.front: transparent material
cards.back: A material that lets light pass through. Glass is used for windows because it is transparent and hard.
cards.say: transparent material. A material that lets light pass through. Glass is used for windows because it is transparent and hard.

cards.front: Why are raincoats made from waterproof materials?
cards.back: Waterproof materials do not let water through, so you stay dry.
cards.say: Why are raincoats made from waterproof materials? Waterproof materials do not let water through, so you stay dry.

cards.front: flexible
cards.back: Able to bend easily without breaking. Rubber is flexible.
cards.say: flexible. Able to bend easily without breaking. Rubber is flexible.

cards.front: Why are tyres made of rubber?
cards.back: Rubber is flexible, grips the road and is strong.
cards.say: Why are tyres made of rubber? Rubber is flexible, grips the road and is strong.

cards.front: melting point
cards.back: The temperature at which a solid turns into a liquid. Different materials have different melting points.
cards.say: melting point. The temperature at which a solid turns into a liquid. Different materials have different melting points.

cards.front: How do you decide which material to use for a job?
cards.back: List the properties the job needs and choose the material whose properties fit best, then test it.
cards.say: How do you decide which material to use for a job? List the properties the job needs and choose the material whose properties fit best, then test it.
